articles.title: YOUR BEST IDEAS SHOULDN'T LIVE EVERYWHERE
articles.summary: You know the drill: ideas in Slack, context buried in docs, and Jira tickets you swear you saw somewhere. That was Maple too. See how they rolled out Jira Product Discovery to get ideas and prioritization into one place, plus the month-by-month playbook they used to go from one team's pilot to an org-wide standard.

articles.title: HOW THE LEADING AI COMPANIES DO PRODUCT
articles.summary: AI makes execution cheaper and experimentation faster, but product expertise still matters. The advantage shifts toward judgment, customer understanding, taste, and verification.

articles.title: IS BEHAVIOURAL SCIENCE BECOMING AI'S NEXT PRODUCT CATEGORY?
articles.summary: AI vendors are increasingly marketing behavioral science, emotional calibration, and conversation design as core capabilities.

articles.title: HOW TO NAME THINGS
articles.summary: Good naming reflects clear thinking. Precise language makes systems easier to understand and can expose deeper design flaws.

articles.title: SLOP-CREEP: WHEN BUILDING GETS CHEAPER THAN THINKING
articles.summary: AI agents have created "slop-creep" - the accumulation of unnecessary features, abstractions, and infrastructure built simply because they are cheap to produce. Without implementation friction, weak ideas survive longer, especially in large companies where software persists.

articles.title: AI CAN CLIMB THE HILL. HUMANS PICK THE NEXT ONE
articles.summary: AI can increasingly handle execution, but humans still choose the next hill to climb. Consumer AI's biggest opportunity may be helping people feel happier and more connected, not merely more productive.

articles.title: APPLIED AI DOESN'T WORK
articles.summary: AI creates little value when it simply speeds up a broken process. Companies should redesign the workflow first, then use software, agents, and humans where each is best suited.
